newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei eases, hurt by Sakakibara's comment.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei eases, hurt by Sakakibara's comment.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were weaker by midday on Thursday following comments by a Japanese Finance Ministry official on Wednesday.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, said the yen's recent decline against the U.S. dollar was excessive and Japan would take decisive action at an appropriate time.
"Dealers are taking that as a hint to a rate hike sometime in June or July," said a dealer with a European institution.
At 0300 GMT, the Nikkei 225 June contract was down 50 points at 17,995 after hitting a high of 18,130 on the back of a firmer Wall Street.
Wall Street ended 92.71 points up on Wednesday at 6,679.87.
Dealers said the market dismissed Japan's trade surplus data for fiscal year 1996/1997 released shortly after the open.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract was trading around 352.4 against its previous close at 357.2.
